verdict:
KILL entry-now, carried as a WATCH gated on the 2026-09-02 print. No escalation trigger fires: benches concordant, no ADVANCE, not held, and the print - the only COMPANY-CONFIRMED date in this entire batch - is 13 sessions out, well outside the 5-trading-day window.

THE SIZING QUESTION IS THE WHOLE CASE, AND BOTH FRAMES ARE DEFENSIBLE FROM THE SAME FILING. At $12.28 on 61.81M shares the cap is $759M and EV about $775M. On the company's frame that is 6.0x adjusted EBITDA ($130M) and looks cheap. On economics it is $130M less roughly $56M of annualised SBC = $74M, so 10.5x - and on actual owner cash, operating cash flow ~$95M less ~$30M capex less $56M SBC is roughly $9M, which is a three-digit multiple. The triage was right that this gap is the sizing decision. What resolves it is that the denominator is not growing: FY27 revenue guidance of $510-520M is +7.2% headline but AccessOne contributes ~$37M in FY27 against a ~$7M FY26 stub, so ORGANIC growth is about +0.9% for the year and about -0.4% across Q2-Q4 - against 5.3% annual dilution (62.04M vs 58.92M diluted). Revenue per share is falling. A 6x multiple on a flat, share-diluting business with a $56M add-back is not cheap; it is the adjusted venue doing the work.

THE UNNARRATED LINE IS WORSE THAN THE NARRATED ONE. Everyone is watching Network Solutions and the FDA advertising crackdown. Meanwhile Subscription and related services fell 3.0% ($52.721M vs $54.355M) on a basis the 10-Q itself certifies as un-reclassified ('prior period amounts have not been reclassified... did not affect any previously reported amounts'), while healthcare-services clients GREW 7% (4,708 vs 4,411). Red read that as core repricing of about -9.4% per client and called it FATAL. Blue reduced it to SIZING and was right to: AHSC growth is land-into-small-practices by design, so revenue per client is mix-confounded, and total revenue per AHSC is actually +6% ($27,811 vs $26,283) with no churn narrative from management to confirm repricing. Blue then found the thing that matters more - the subscription erosion PREDATES the FDA shock, beginning sequentially in mid-FY26 ($54.355M -> $53.702M). That is a second, independent problem the cohort narrative does not cover at all.

THE CHANNEL ANALYSIS IS GENUINELY GOOD AND IT STILL DOES NOT BUY THE STOCK. The triage's best work: the FDA's proposed rule eliminating the 'adequate provision' option applies to BROADCAST DTC advertising, and killing broadcast economics should REDIRECT pharma dollars toward measurable non-broadcast channels, of which point-of-care is the purest - so on the rule itself PHR is a share-gainer, not a victim. What actually hit is the other prong: ~100 cease-and-desist letters plus thousands of untitled letters lengthening legal review and shortening brand commitment windows. Management's own language is a visibility symptom, not a demand symptom - 'shorter visibility into spending commitments', clients 'committing lower spend levels for the second half', and explicitly 'we do not believe these developments are signaling a structural shift in demand'. That distinction is real and it is exactly the kind of channel error worth harvesting into the graph. But a budgeting-cycle effect and a demand-destruction effect look identical for two quarters, and the divergence does not resolve until the September print at the earliest.

THE OWNERSHIP LEG FLIPPED TWICE AND ENDS BEARISH. The triage said Pale Fire was flat at a pre-cut basis. Red REFUTED that and did so against its own case, honestly: Pale Fire added $18.3M at $11.15-11.69 in mid-March and another $10.4M at $7.78-8.53 post-cut, reaching 8,924,329 shares / 14.7% at a blended ~$11.60. Doubling down with the new guide in hand is a real bull datum. Then blue closed the coverage gap red left open: there is NO 13D/A after 2026-04-02, and a >=1% add would compel an amendment, so Pale Fire has NOT materially accumulated June through August. Red's own change-my-mind condition (c) is therefore answered NO. At $12.28 you are paying about +47% over the activist's LATEST purchases, and the filing flags possible margin-loan funding. Net: the informed holder stopped buying four months ago, well below here.

So: +58% off the $7.77 low, at a level that offers no discount to a materially worse outlook, into a dated binary 13 sessions away. Better sized after the guide reaction than raced into it.

court.record: batch4 8/15; red 7/blue 8 SUSTAINED with two reductions and one corrected trigger - outcome CONCORDANT. Blue downgraded red's FATAL to SIZING on a causal overreach, corrected red's own re-entry threshold, and CLOSED a coverage gap in a way that strengthened the kill.

reopen_gates: EVENT (primary, dated): the 2026-09-02 print. Four gates, all of which must be read together rather than singly - (a) is the $510-520M FY27 guide held or cut; (b) what is the 2H COMMITTED-spend language, which is the actual leading variable; (c) Subscription against the CORRECT comp of $53.7M - NOT red's $54.4M, which was the wrong quarter - with AHSC mix commentary; (d) Network Solutions against the +24.7% comp, where guide-consistent is about $34M, >= $37M breaks the structural read and < $32M confirms it.

DATA: management quantifying the subscription decline as deliberate bundling migration rather than repricing. Total revenue per AHSC at +6% leaves this genuinely open, and it is the difference between a mix effect and core erosion.
FLOW: confirmed Pale Fire accumulation resuming (a 13D/A would compel disclosure). Absent since 2026-04-02.

BUILD (do this BEFORE the print, not after): instrument scheduler_exhaust - a fixed panel of PHR-client online booking pages, tracking days-to-next-available as a leading read on visit volume into payments and subscription. Red identified it as the one genuinely applicable connector and it is currently UNCHECKABLE for want of a panel, not for want of a mechanism.
